Mika+FileScope reads the names, sizes and modification dates of files on your Desktop to show how much space each file type uses there — for example, that 340 screenshots take up 12 GB. File contents are read only when you start a duplicate search, and only on this Mac. Nothing is moved, changed, deleted or uploaded.

Mika+FileScope reads the names, sizes and modification dates of files in your Documents folder to group them by type and show which ones use the most space — for example, which PDFs have not been touched in over a year. File contents are read only when you start a duplicate search, and only on this Mac. Nothing is moved, changed, deleted or uploaded.

Mika+FileScope reads the names, sizes and modification dates of files in your Downloads folder to report what is still sitting there — for example, 18 installer disk images using 9 GB. File contents are read only when you start a duplicate search, and only on this Mac. Nothing is moved, changed, deleted or uploaded.

Mika+FileScope reads the names, sizes and modification dates of files on a connected external drive to show which file types fill it — for example, that video files use 80 percent of a backup disk. Access is read-only: nothing is written to the drive, and nothing is uploaded.

Mika+FileScope reads the names, sizes and modification dates of files on a network share you choose to scan, to show which file types use the most space there — for example, which project folder on a shared server grew the fastest. Access is read-only: nothing is written to the share, and nothing is uploaded.

Mika+FileScope reads the names, sizes and modification dates of files in cloud folders such as iCloud Drive so they can be included in the size report — for example, that a synced Documents folder holds 4 GB of video. Files stay in the cloud: they are not downloaded, changed or removed.
